Subject: Hosted API SLOs — p50/p95 measurement window ask

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput looked great. Before we sign the contract we need one last ask from our compliance and platform teams around how p50/p95 are computed for the Hosted API.

TL;DR: Our infra team runs tight end-of-day batch jobs that create short spikes. They want p95 to be insensitive to very short, high-variance microbursts (1–3 minutes) but still reflect sustained degradation. Can Redwood provide an exception that uses a rolling-percentile aggregation (short-window percentiles aggregated into an hourly p95) rather than a single large-window raw percentile?

Attached is a short doc with our traffic profile (finoptics-slo-request-20260810.pdf). If we can agree on an approach and add it as an SLO addendum, procurement is ready to move fast.

Specific asks:
- p50 commitment: 150ms (standard) — keep as-is.
- p95 commitment: 450ms, but computed using a rolling-percentile scheme that reduces sensitivity to 1–3 minute spikes.
- Measurement/reporting cadence: hourly reporting, but raw telemetry must be retained for 30 days for audits.

Can you loop in engineering for feasibility and a short note on how this affects our SLA credits calculation?

Thanks,
Adam Reyes
Head of Platform Engineering
FinOptics

Hi Adam — thanks for the clear note and the traffic profile. Appreciate the heads-up on the batch spikes.

Quick summary from our side: conceptually we can support a rolling-percentile aggregation for p95 reporting. That means computing short-window percentiles (we generally use 5-minute windows for high-fidelity telemetry) and then aggregating those windows into an hourly reported p95, which reduces the impact of isolated 1–3 minute microbursts.

I’ve looped in Marissa (SRE/product) and Dylan (sales engineering) to flag impact on SLA crediting and contractual language. Two items we need to confirm:
1) Retention: you asked for 30-day raw telemetry — that’s fine under Hosted but we’ll note it as part of the addendum.
2) Credits calculation: our default SLA crediting is based on raw p95 across the billing window — we’ll need an exception clause that defines the rolling-percentile aggregation as the contract measurement for p95 in the hosted environment.

We’ll propose a draft addendum and a short technical note on how the metric is computed (window size, aggregator, tie-breaker logic). Expect a draft by Friday.

Adam — looping in the technical detail you asked for. Dylan and I discussed implementation and crediting options.

Proposal (technical):
- Short-window computation: compute per-route latency percentiles every 5 minutes (p50 and p95 for each 5m window).
- Aggregation rule: for hourly reporting, rank the 5-minute p95 values within the hour and take the weighted 95th percentile across the 12 windows (equivalent to computing p95 over the concatenated samples but with reduced sensitivity to single-window outliers). In practice this behaves like a "rolling-percentile" approach and dampens 1–3 minute spikes.
- Credit calculation: SLA credits will be evaluated against the aggregated hourly p95 for the SLO period (monthly). If the aggregated p95 exceeds the contractual threshold for more than N hours in the month (we suggest N=3 for enterprise customers), then crediting applies per contract.

Operational notes:
- We will keep raw request telemetry for 30 days (as Adam requested) for audit and debug.
- For transparency, we’ll publish hourly p95 and the underlying 5-minute p95 series to a shared dashboard (read-only link) so your SREs can validate behavior.
- Edge case: sustained high latency across >30 minutes will be visible in both the 5-minute series and the hourly aggregate; the rolling-percentile does not mask prolonged degradation.

Next steps:
1) If this model looks acceptable, we’ll issue an SLO addendum draft and a short appendix that defines the math/aggregation functions.
2) Dylan — can you confirm whether this changes any rate-limiting or burst policies we discussed previously?

Adam — happy to hop on a 20-minute sync to walk through a quick example chart.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product SRE | Redwood Inference
